newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish PM likely to survive no-confidence move.
newsitem.headline: Swedish PM likely to survive no-confidence move.

text.p: Swedish Prime Minister Goran Persson looked certain on Wednesday to survive any no-confidence vote over China policy after two out of six non-government parties said they would abstain or support him.
Three Swedish opposition parties said earlier they would seek a no-confidence vote in parliament over the Social Democrat leader's comments during a visit to China when he appeared to praise Beijing.
The Conservative, Liberal and Christian Democratic parties announced they would file a bid for the vote after a special parliamentary debate.
The Leftist party said it would support Persson while the Environmental Party said it would abstain in any no-confidence vote on the issue.
Late Wednesday afternoon the Centre Party was still meeting to decide its stance.
Persson angered Swedish politicians during an official visit to Beijing this month when he made what were seen to be complimentary remarks about China's political stability.
The ensuing row prompted a meeting of the foreign policy advisory committee, chaired by the king, and Wednesday's debate in parliament.
Persson, leader of the ruling Social Democratic Party, became Prime Minister in March this year, replacing Ingvar Carlsson.
He heads a minority government which survives with the support of the Leftist Party, but he has been moving towards forming a coalition with the Centre Party.

Liberal party member Lars Leijonborg told Reuters: "It looks unlikely that there will be a majority (for no-confidence). But even a majority of no-confidence votes and abstentions would be a severe check on the government."
